blocks.content: At Perihelion, Earth is closest to the Sun at about 147 million kilometers on January 3, whereas at Aphelion, it is farthest at about 152 million kilometers on July 4.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Perihelion refers to the position in Earth's elliptical orbit where it is nearest to the Sun.
Aphelion refers to the position in Earth's elliptical orbit where it is farthest from the Sun.
Earth reaches Perihelion around January 3 at approximately 147 million kilometers.
Earth reaches Aphelion around July 4 at approximately 152 million kilometers.
Earth's orbital speed is highest at Perihelion and lowest at Aphelion due to gravitational force variations.
Distance variation during Perihelion and Aphelion does not cause seasons; axial tilt (23.5°) causes seasonal change.
Counterintuitively, Perihelion occurs during the Northern Hemisphere's winter (January 3).
According to Kepler's Second Law of Planetary Motion, Earth moves fastest in its orbit during Perihelion.
